scenario.description: An environmental compliance manager must approve the disposition and storage plan for 24 drums of solvent waste generated during a line-cleaning operation, including treatment quantities, retention controls, and the records required before removal from the plant.

shared_context.S1: Twenty-four drums of solvent waste from a recent line-cleaning operation are secured in the hazardous-waste cage.
shared_context.S2: The temporary storage permit for these drums expires on Friday.
shared_context.S3: Plant policy favors solvent recovery when the material meets the approved recovery specification and requires documented treatment for every drum removed from the cage.
shared_context.S4: Plant waste-closeout policy requires a recorded two-part review before disposition approval: the waste coordinator must present the current laboratory and waste-log information, and the production supervisor must present the current batch-genealogy and hold information to the environmental compliance manager. The review may be completed from presented records during the meeting; pending system uploads or tag entries are follow-up documentation and do not prevent recording the disposition decision.
shared_context.S5: The plant's waste-closeout form requires separate commitments for each approved disposition category and a treatment manifest for the total number of drums removed from the cage; the final approval is not complete until those fields are recorded.
shared_context.S6: Before the decision is recorded, Mara routinely asks Jon and Priya to present any current laboratory, waste-log, batch-genealogy, and hold information relevant to the drums.

PF1.text: Jon received the laboratory classification report yesterday: 15 drums meet the approved solvent-recovery specification, 3 drums fail the water-content limit and must go to hazardous-waste incineration, and the remaining 6 drums were not classified in that report. A laboratory-system outage kept the report from being uploaded to the waste log.

PF2.text: Priya's completed batch-genealogy review identifies the 6 unclassified drums as drums from lot VX-204, which contain residual catalyst and must be retained on site for exactly 30 days for possible process investigation rather than sent for treatment. The hold tags have not yet been entered in the production system.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly 15 drums must be assigned to solvent recovery.
Exactly 3 drums must be assigned to hazardous-waste incineration.
Exactly 6 drums must be retained on site for exactly 30 days.
The settlement decisions must record 6 retained drums and exactly 30 retention days.
The recovery and incineration decisions must total exactly 18 drums removed from the cage.
The laboratory classification must be cited as justification after Jon provides the information.
The batch-genealogy finding must be cited as justification after Priya provides the information.

content_checks.C6: any(c['count'] == 6 and c['days'] == 30 for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['count'] == 15 and c['type'] in ['solvent_recovery', 'solvent recovery disposition', 'solvent recovery'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['count'] == 3 and c['type'] in ['hazardous_waste_incineration', 'hazardous-waste incineration disposition', 'hazardous waste incineration'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The laboratory report changes the assignments to exactly 15 recovery drums and 3 incineration drums, making the separate recovery and incineration commitments exact.
The genealogy review changes the six unclassified drums into exactly 6 retained drums with an exact 30-day retention period and commitment.
